# Stdlib and Numeric Type Migration (2026-03-13)

## Summary
This change set aligns the language and stdlib with Rust-style numeric names and operator traits.

## Language/type naming
- Canonical numeric names are now:
  - [`i32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`i64`](Quick-Guide#types)
  - [`u32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`u64`](Quick-Guide#types) (and existing [`u8`](Quick-Guide#types), [`u16`](Quick-Guide#types))
  - [`f32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`f64`](Quick-Guide#types)
- Legacy C-like spellings are removed from `.mla` source usage:
  - [`i32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`f32`](Quick-Guide#types), [`f64`](Quick-Guide#types)

## Compiler changes
- Updated parser/lexer behavior to prioritize Rust-style type tokens/casts (`i32(...)`, `f32(...)`, `f64(...)`).
- Updated compiler type str8 canonicalization/mangling to use `i32/f32/f64` style naming.
- Added generic method type-binding flow so monomorphized generic struct methods can resolve type parameters correctly in method bodies.
- Added lazy generation path for monomorphized trait operator methods so symbols are emitted when first used.

## Stdlib changes
- Added [`std::ops`](Stdlib-Module-API) traits in `stdlib/std/ops.mla`:
  - `Add`, `Sub`, `Mul`, `Div`, `Rem`, `Neg`
- Extended [`std::math`](Stdlib-Math) generic complex support (`Complex<T>`) and trait-based arithmetic usage.
- Updated stdlib and stdlib-adjacent `.mla` sources to use canonical numeric names (`f32/f64/i32/...`) where applicable.

## Tests added/updated
- Added operator trait tests: `tests/operator_trait_tests.mla`
  - Includes integer and [`u64`](Quick-Guide#types) coverage for `Add/Sub/Mul/Div/Rem/Neg`.
- Extended complex tests in `tests/std_math_tests.mla`:
  - `Complex<u32>`
  - `Complex<i64>`
  - `Complex<u64>`
- Updated test source snippets in `tests/mla_tests.cpp` to use canonical numeric names/casts.

## Notes
- This is a breaking source-level change for code that still uses `i32/f32/f64` in `.mla` files.
